children: Samsung Electronics (SSNLF), the Korean semiconductor and consumer-electronics titan, tumbled approximately 4% to 250,500 won Wednesday as renewed U.S.-Iran strikes pushed Brent crude toward $95 and ripped through Asian markets. South Korea's KOSPI also dropped roughly 4%. Investors were not debating Samsung's execution. They were fleeing technology stocks as expensive oil revived the nightmare combination of hotter inflation, higher rates and shrinking valuations.

That panic slammed straight into a wall of profit. Samsung's second-quarter results showed nearly 171 trillion won in consolidated revenue and approximately 89.4 trillion won in operating profit. The semiconductor engine dominated, generating 127.5 trillion won in revenue and 89.2 trillion won in operating profit as explosive AI-memory demand collided with tight supply and drove prices higher.

The picture tells the fundamental story clearly: Samsung's GF Score stands at an elite 90 out of 100, backed by exceptional profitability, growth and financial strength, although weaker GF Value and middling momentum readings flash a valuation warning. Samsung delivered the earnings. Investors delivered the selloff. When oil surges and interest-rate fears return, even monster semiconductor profits cannot protect the multiple.

title: Samsung Loses 4% as $95 Oil Hits Its AI-Memory Rally
